cs.t: Wow, glad to hear it! Here's some other products you might appreciate: * The latest is these giant sun hats, especially ones which drape over the back of the neck.[0] Search for fishing/boating hats. * Lots of cheap sunglasses from the dollar store (ahem, "tree" in my area). The avalanche ensures I always have a pair. No worse than the $10-20 versions, and I don't care when I inevitably lose/break them. * The thick (black) gloves from Harbor Freight are quite nice. Effectively reusable. * Back at the aforementioned dollar store, they sell 100-packs of thin disposable food service gloves. LIFE CHANGING for pumping gas. Literally gloves in the glove box haha. * If you have feet, get yourself some Powerstep insoles. If you go to a podiatrist it's the first thing they do anyway. Feet matter. * For wildfire/campfire/dusty activities/viruses, I pull out  this dorky thing .[1] Its dorkiness is exceeded only by its effectiveness. :) I gave tips about using it here.[2] * For air filtration, I'm a big fan of the Filtrete 1900 (MERV 13) filters. Low restriction, and just the "sweet spot" of efficiency vs airflow. I put them in my HVAC system — some restriction yes, but much better than others! Also great for "Corsi box" DIY filters. * I grab cheap foam earplugs (Harbor Fright again) and cut them in half. Industrial modernity is surprisingly loud — as it turns out hearing loss isn't a 'natural' part of aging, it's all just environmental exposure. I keep a few in that useless little pants
cs.th: Titanium spikes kill superbugs drug-free by ripping them apart
